You cannot write msgs right away here https://github.com/Fenoman/odyssey/commit/bc045814b66a3bb78af65b0c6132b4dea4306fe8#diff-d23e9ec6d450d0487f0e95425e6eaea8e76945e520a720a69cf0efd2cc0403dcR1183
because of pipe-lining. You need to wait for all preceding msgs to reach client first. This can be achieved using OD_REQ_SYNC. I did small refactoring in https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/commit/b69c18c616d14e1b501afeec581433984b8c6966 to showcase this.

For example, for prepared statement in tx pool support we use OD_REQ_SYNC here https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/b69c18c616d14e1b501afeec581433984b8c6966/sources/frontend.c#L1213
This way we send parse complete msgs only after replying to all prev msgs in pipe

First of all, thank you for the detailed feedback on my previous patch!
I realize now that I’d overlooked an important detail in the sync-point logic—sorry for this 😊.

I have pushed a new revision to my fork https://github.com/Fenoman/odyssey/commit/d32ab1d39c54c177793f1961ea31e4f679a3296e. Key changes:

1. **Sync-point handling**  
   `OD_REQ_SYNC` can now be returned in two distinct situations:
   * the original reserve-prepared-statement path (where `server->parse_msg` is set), and
   * the new _ignore-DISCARD-ALL_ path (where no `parse_msg` is generated).  
  
   Because of that I replaced the hard assertion:
    ```C
    assert(server->parse_msg != NULL);
    ```
   with a conditional block:
    ```C 
    if (server->parse_msg) {
        /* fill internals structs in */
        if (od_frontend_deploy_prepared_stmt_msg(...
    }
    ```
   This keeps the old behaviour intact and avoids an abort() when `parse_msg` is legitimately `NULL` for the `DISCARD ALL`. 
2. **Packet ordering**  
   The virtual _CommandComplete + ReadyForQuery_ message is now stored in `server->sync_point_deploy_msg`.  
   The main loop flushes it right after the sync-point, so pipelining is preserved.
3. **Cache invalidation**  
   `server->prep_stmts` is only cleared when a real `DISCARD …` reaches PostgreSQL.  
   When we intercept `DISCARD ALL`, prepared statements remain valid.

Btw, regarding **SPQR**—would it be possible to implement both the existing `pool_discard_query` feature and the new `pool_ignore_discardall` option there as well?  

`pool_discard_query` is extremely useful in certain cases—for example, cleaning up `pgv` variables (`pg_variables` extension), because they can be cleared **ONLY** by calling `SELECT pgv_free();`.

We’re planning to experiment with sharding some of our databases, and having these features available in **SPQR** is essential for us.

Hi rkhapov,

Thanks for reviewing my patch!

The issue I'm addressing is a potential NULL pointer dereference in the `auth.c` file when accessing `client->received_password.password` or `client->password.password` without sufficient prior validation. In some cases, if `client == NULL` or those fields are not set, this can lead to undefined behavior or crashes during authentication flow.

This change ensures that all accesses to these fields are guarded by checks on `client` and its subfields before they're used. The logic has been simplified and centralized to avoid redundant NULL checks and make the code safer.

I believe the fix is important for stability, especially under edge conditions like malformed client credentials or missing password data due to misconfiguration or network issues.

Best regards,
Eugeny Goryachev

hi!

this is complex question, we allow odyssey to be not thread safe in some scenarios, specifically in the application closing cases, where thread safety is not critical (ofc we work to fix this too, but with low priority)

in other cases we try our best to make odyssey thread safe, for example, right now we are working at thread sanitizer tests and support https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/pull/901

so, if you experienced some problems, you could create an issue (or use this one) with detailed information about the subj (the best option is coredump file)

now about your questions:
1. od_router_close and od_backend_close solves different tasks, so there is no race or double free
2. hashmap is split on backets, every backet has its own mutex
3. channels has a sleep lock to manage critical section, so many thread can access channel simultaneously and this is not a problem (if you have case where channel doesnt work correctly, add some details please)
